shared_constraints: The full 10-segment suite must stay green, and EVERY segment runs as its own tool call - a monolithic invocation nears the 10-minute tool ceiling and a kill reads as a false red.

spec_loop_guard.py must stay at or above its per-file coverage floor of 86. It measures 92.0% (127/138) today, the TIGHTEST margin in PER_FILE_FLOORS and the only one annotated 'kept at v1 floor', so roughly 6 points of headroom against real new line count. Anything added inside main() is measured; coverage_omit.txt exempts only the two-line __main__ shim and test_measure_coverage_manifest.py pins its size. New gate code MUST be covered.
spec_loop_guard.py is standard-library only. Keep it that way.

Do not invert the guard's fail-open-on-internal-error doctrine: an unexpected exception must still ALLOW the action, even for a gate whose job is to block. The alternative is a crashed guard wedging every turn end in every session on the machine. But make it fail open PER RUN, not with one try around the whole loop: with two active runs, a broken dag.json in run A must not fail open for run B. An .active marker with no dag.json is a REACHABLE state - find_active_runs tolerates it - and dag.load_dag raises DagError on it.

Branch on payload['hook_event_name'] BEFORE the tool dispatch in evaluate()/main(). A Stop payload carries NO tool_name key, so an implementation written as `if tool == "Stop"` passes every evaluate() unit test and never fires live. This is the single most likely way this run ships a silent no-op.

The Stop block needs its OWN emit path: top-level {"decision": "block", "reason": ...} on stdout, empirically confirmed this run. Reusing main()'s existing hookSpecificOutput shape produces a malformed block that is ignored, which reads as allow.

Judge runnability on next_wave's slice_ids being non-empty - NEVER on the absence of a 'done' key. next_wave returns {'index', 'slice_ids': [], 'deadlock': True} with no 'done' key at all, so `if not report.get('done')` would block both the deadlock escalation question and the Phase-5 publish prompt.

Import dag and run_state rather than re-reading dag.json: a second copy of next_wave would fork the split-parent readiness rule (a split parent is terminal; a dep on one is satisfied only when its children are recursively satisfied; a childless split parent is a deadlock, not a stall). Use FUNCTION-LOCAL imports inside the new gate paths only, so the Bash and Write hot paths keep their current cost and behaviour, in the try/import/except ImportError -> None form used at dashboard_server.py:74-89, and fail open on ImportError or DagError. Measured cost: 14ms to import both, 34ms total against a synthetic 4.5MB events file (20x the largest real run) against a 5-second budget.
Apply the controller-session narrowing ONLY to the new Stop gate - never to check_bash or check_write, whose Task-subagent coverage is a verified 2026-07-07 property of the guard.

.paused must allow ONLY the new gate. Do NOT thread it through find_active_runs(): if a paused run reads as non-blocking there, pausing silently unlocks push-before-publish, broad staging and commit-on-the-default-branch. A stale .paused is a silent permanent loss of the gate and deserves the same remediation treatment as a stale .active.

Every denial or block text names BOTH the compliant alternative and the stale-marker remediation, matching the existing _remediation() sentence. The Stop reason additionally names the literal .paused escape path and carries an 'if you are not the controller' clause. Put the visible-trace requirement in the FIRST-fire reason text: if the controller is deliberately stopping, its next message must say why, so the transcript carries it. Do NOT append to a log file under docs/spec-loop/<run-id>/ - an untracked file there dirties the tree and collides with the Phase-1 clean-tree guard.
The module docstring of spec_loop_guard.py opens 'PreToolUse guard' and becomes false the moment a Stop branch lands. Update it in the same change.

Add no new runtime .py script, no new *.test.mjs harness module, and no new command, agent or skill: test_doctrine_run_docs.py pins all of those counts in plugins/spec-loop/README.md against a real count on disk. A new test_*.py file is free - the script count excludes test_-prefixed files.

Exactly ONE prose count moves: escalation-gate SKILL.md:128 'Three things that look like stopping points' becomes four. Line 79 opens a DIFFERENT list (budget-exhausted, internal-error, the over-scope flag) and must not be touched. The tail clause 'exactly the six triggers above' at SKILL.md:129 is PINNED by test_doctrine_refactor_scope.py and must survive the edit verbatim.
Never write an artifact claiming a gate enforces something whose firing was not empirically established. Only the Stop gate's firing and its per-turn re-arming are proven.
The installed plugin is 2.2.0 while this repo is 2.3.0, so nothing this run adds to hooks.json protects this run. No artifact may imply otherwise, and no test will notice.

Emit any prose that quotes a git command through the Write/Edit tools, never a shell heredoc: the guard's own command-text patterns match the quoted example and deny the write. Observed live twice at this run's intake. Do NOT narrow those patterns to dodge quoted text - that would weaken the real guard; use the non-shell write path instead.
scope_ceiling: GATE A - the PreToolUse gate on AskUserQuestion. Dropped by human decision at the intake round: its firing is unverified on 2.1.260, it would deny the controller's own dirty-tree escalation on the --resume path, and it breaks /spec-loop:knowledge-graph's opt-in prompt. Build no part of it, and register nothing for it.
The loop-boundary audit event and its run-state-v2.md event type - deferred by the human when choosing 'Gates + prose' over 'Gates + prose + audit event'.

Registering SubagentStop. Guardian found SubagentStop is a distinct event name in the 2.1.260 binary, so registering only Stop most likely leaves slice implementers ungated - which is correct. Telling an implementer to 'continue Phase 2 step 1' would be role confusion.
Narrowing check_bash's or check_write's existing command-text patterns for any reason, including the quoted-text false positive observed this run.
Any change to slice-wave.workflow.js, dag.py, run_state.py or worktrees.py LOGIC. The gate imports from dag.py and run_state.py; it does not modify them.
Fixing Phase 5's marker-vs-commit ordering, the reason runs orphan their completion markers. Recorded as deferred; the gitignore work in s3 removes the symptom, not the cause.
A new standalone hook script. The gate lives in spec_loop_guard.py.
Any release or version bump. This lands under CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

Remediate two P2 defects s1's review recorded against the new escalation-ordering paragraph in plugins/spec-loop/commands/spec-loop.md, and tighten the pin that should have caught them. (1) The paragraph mandates an `escalation-opened` event before any controller-originated AskUserQuestion but never mandates the matching `escalation-answered` write-back. `run_state.open_escalations()` treats any opened id with no answer event as OPEN forever, so a question recorded under this rule - a decomposition ambiguity, a config first-run choice, the Phase-5 publish prompt - is re-gathered by Phase 2 step 7 and re-asked at the next wave boundary, and dashboard_server.py keeps surfacing it. State the write-back as the second half of the same ordering rule, in the same voice. (2) The paragraph's closing sentence currently reads 'This excludes records a wave raised are already appended by `persist-slice` - never re-append those', which fuses an exclusion clause with a declarative one so the reader cannot tell whether wave-raised records are excluded from the rule or merely described. Rewrite it to say plainly what it means: records a wave raised are already appended by `persist-slice`, so the rule does not apply to them and they must never be re-appended. The existing lowercase substring pin in test_doctrine_loop_boundary.py must still pass - the reviewer confirmed a grammatical phrasing satisfies it; adjust the pin only if it genuinely cannot. (3) Fix the orphan ~51-column line the insertion left mid-paragraph, wrapping to the file's ~90-column convention. (4) In test_doctrine_loop_boundary.py, make `test_the_markers_are_stated_once_to_be_uncommitted` actually assert the sentence appears exactly once rather than merely present, since duplicate-claim drift is the risk it names, and add the new write-back sentence to the pinned set. Do not touch any other file, and do not re-litigate s1's design.

Two narrow fixes, nothing else. (1) In plugins/spec-loop/scripts/spec_loop_guard.py, `_controller_marker` catches only OSError, so an undecodable `.controller-session` raises UnicodeDecodeError (a ValueError, not an OSError), escapes the per-run try structure and is caught only by main()'s blanket handler - failing open for the whole loop instead of for that run. Widen it to catch ValueError as well, matching its sibling readers `_blocking_slices` and `_has_open_escalation` which already do, and add a test writing undecodable bytes to the marker that asserts the gate still blocks for a SECOND, healthy active run in the same project - the per-run isolation is the property under test, not merely the absence of a crash. (2) In plugins/spec-loop/commands/spec-loop.md, the escalation-ordering paragraph now ends 'The rule does not apply to wave-raised escalations: records a wave raised are already appended by `persist-slice`, so never re-append those.' Read literally that exempts wave-raised escalations from the escalation-answered write-back too, which is wrong: Phase 2 step 7 writes answers back for ALL open escalations and open_escalations() holds any opened id open until its answered event lands, so following it literally would leave every wave-raised escalation open forever. Scope the exemption to the APPEND half only, in one sentence, keeping the paragraph's voice and the ~90-column wrap; extend the pin in test_doctrine_loop_boundary.py so the narrower scope is asserted rather than assumed. Change nothing else, and do not re-litigate the design of s1, s2 or s5.
